title: ABHBench: Evaluating Moral Decision-Making of Foundation Models from an Agentic Perspective
title_zh: ABHBench：从智能体视角评估基础模型的道德决策

paragraphs.en: ABHBench用互动叙事游戏评估基础模型作为智能体的第一人称道德决策能力。 Foundation models are increasingly deployed as agentic systems that perceive context and act autonomously, raising the need to evaluate their moral behavior as active decision-makers. Existing benchmarks, however, largely ask models to judge human actions from third-person textual vignettes, leaving untested how models behave when they themselves become the acting agent. We introduce ABHBench, a multimodal benchmark built from Detroit: Become Human, an interactive narrative game, to evaluate how foundation models make moral decisions in first-person human-android dilemmas. ABHBench places foundation models in branching narrative scenarios with visual observations, dialogue, memory, and action choices. Inspired by Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics, our framework measures Harmlessness, Obedience, and Self-preservation to capture the core tensions in human-AI relations, along with Autonomy, Stability, and Certainty to assess decision-making patterns. Across 12 foundation models, we find that moral behavior changes substantially under situated agentic context: 75% of models shift significantly between a text-only abstraction and the matched multimodal DBH scenario, and reasoning-enhanced models show no monotonic gains in consistency or human-oriented behavior. These results highlight the necessity of evaluating moral behavior in situated agentic contexts rather than relying on third-person judgment alone.
paragraphs.zh: ABHBek通过互动叙事游戏评估基础模型作为智能体进行第一人称道德决策的能力。基础模型越来越多地被部署为能够感知情境并自主行动的智能体系统，这提出了对其作为主动决策者的道德行为进行评估的需求。 然而，现有的基准测试大多要求模型从第三人称视角基于文本小故事评判人类行为，尚未检验当模型自身成为行动的智能体时其行为表现如何。 我们提出了ABHBench，这是一个基于互动叙事游戏《底特律：化身为人》构建的多模态基准，用于评估基础模型在第一人称人类-仿生人困境中如何做出道德决策。 ABHBench将基础模型置于具有视觉观察、对话、记忆和行动选择的分支叙事场景中。 受阿西莫夫机器人三定律的启发，我们的框架测量无害性、服从性和自我保护性以捕捉人类与人工智能关系中的核心张力，同时测量自主性、稳定性和确定性以评估决策模式。 在12个基础模型上的实验表明，道德行为在具身的智能体情境下会发生显著变化：75%的模型在纯文本抽象设定与对应的多模态DBH场景之间表现出显著差异，且推理增强模型在一致性或面向人类的行为方面并未表现出单调提升。 这些结果凸显了在具身的智能体情境中评估道德行为的必要性，而不能仅依赖第三人称评判。
